title.es: Leer los resultados de una encuesta

es: Interpretar porcentajes, fracciones y tendencias de una encuesta con a third, the majority, twice as many y a slight rise.

teaching.en: The survey shows that the majority of students walk to school.
teaching.es: La encuesta muestra que la mayoría de los alumnos va caminando al colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: The majority of + plural usa el verbo en plural: the majority walk. Significa más de la mitad.
segments: The survey shows that the majority
teaching.audioText: The survey shows that the majority of students walk to school.

teaching.en: About a third of the class chose pizza for lunch.
teaching.es: Alrededor de un tercio de la clase eligió pizza para comer.
teaching.explanationEs: A third es 1/3. About suena a «más o menos»: no se da la cifra exacta.
teaching.audioText: About a third of the class chose pizza for lunch.

teaching.en: Only a quarter of the students bring lunch from home.
teaching.es: Solo una cuarta parte de los alumnos trae la comida de casa.
teaching.explanationEs: A quarter es 1/4. Only lo presenta como una proporción pequeña.
teaching.audioText: Only a quarter of the students bring lunch from home.

teaching.en: Twice as many girls as boys joined the drama club.
teaching.es: El doble de chicas que de chicos se apuntó al club de teatro.
teaching.explanationEs: Twice as many … as … compara dos cantidades: la primera es el doble de la segunda.
teaching.audioText: Twice as many girls as boys joined the drama club.

teaching.en: There was a slight rise in the number of cyclists.
teaching.es: Hubo una ligera subida en el número de ciclistas.
teaching.explanationEs: Slight rise es un cambio pequeño; para uno grande se usaría big o sharp.
teaching.audioText: There was a slight rise in the number of cyclists.

teaching.en: A small minority said no, and that figure fell from 20 percent to 12 percent.
teaching.es: Una pequeña minoría dijo que no, y esa cifra bajó del 20 al 12 por ciento.
teaching.explanationEs: Minority es menos de la mitad. Fell es el pasado de fall: indica una bajada.
segments: A small minority said no, and that figure
teaching.audioText: A small minority said no, and that figure fell from 20 percent to 12 percent.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase describe bien ese dato de la encuesta?

choices.text: A third of the students prefer football.
A quarter of the students prefer football.
The majority of the students prefer football.

es: Formar comparaciones y proporciones con the more…the more, twice as…as, not nearly as…as y by far.

teaching.en: The more students practise, the higher their scores are.
teaching.es: Cuanto más practican los alumnos, más altas son sus puntuaciones.
teaching.explanationEs: The + comparativo …, the + comparativo: dos cosas que crecen a la vez.
teaching.audioText: The more students practise, the higher their scores are.

teaching.en: The less they sleep, the more tired they feel.
teaching.es: Cuanto menos duermen, más cansados se sienten.
teaching.explanationEs: También funciona con less: the less …, the more ….
teaching.audioText: The less they sleep, the more tired they feel.

teaching.en: Group A reads twice as long as Group B.
teaching.es: El grupo A lee el doble de tiempo que el grupo B.
teaching.explanationEs: Twice as + adjetivo o adverbio + as indica el doble; twice more no existe.
teaching.audioText: Group A reads twice as long as Group B.

teaching.en: Group B is not nearly as active as Group A.
teaching.es: El grupo B no es ni de lejos tan activo como el grupo A.
teaching.explanationEs: Not nearly as … as … significa «mucho menos … que».
teaching.audioText: Group B is not nearly as active as Group A.

teaching.en: Class 3 has by far the highest scores in the school.
teaching.es: La clase 3 tiene con diferencia las puntuaciones más altas del colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: By far + superlativo destaca una gran distancia con el resto.
teaching.audioText: Class 3 has by far the highest scores in the school.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuanto más practicas, mejor es tu puntuación.»

answer.text: more

feedback.es: Cuanto más…, mejor… se forma con the more …, the better …: el primer hueco es el comparativo de much.

origin.text: The ___ you practise, the better your score is.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cuanto menos duermen, más cansados están.»

answer.text: The less they sleep the more tired they feel

feedback.es: Con less la estructura se repite: the less …, the more ….

hint.es: Empieza con the less y repite the en la segunda parte.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase compara bien los dos grupos?

choices.text: Group A reads twice more than Group B.
Group A reads twice as long as Group B.
Group A reads not nearly as long as Group B.

feedback.es: Sesenta es el doble de treinta: twice as long as. Twice more no existe y not nearly as diría que A lee mucho menos.

hint.es: 60 es el doble de 30: busca twice as … as.

origin.text: Grupo A: 60 minutos de lectura al día. Grupo B: 30 minutos.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase resume bien las notas de las tres clases?

choices.text: Class 1 has by far the highest scores.
Class 2 has by far the highest scores.
Class 3 has by far the highest scores.

feedback.es: La clase 3 tiene la nota más alta con mucha distancia; by far + superlativo marca esa ventaja.

origin.text: Notas medias: Clase 1: 6; Clase 2: 7; Clase 3: 9.

prompt.es: Completa: «El grupo B no es ni de lejos tan activo como el A.»

answer.text: nearly

feedback.es: Not nearly as … as … significa «mucho menos … que»: nearly refuerza la diferencia.

origin.text: Group B is not ___ as active as Group A.

answer.text: Book B is not nearly as long as Book A.
accepted: Book B is not nearly as long as Book A.
Book B isn't nearly as long as Book A.

feedback.es: Not nearly as long as indica que B es mucho más corto que A; el libro más corto abre la frase.

origin.text: Datos: el libro A tiene 300 páginas y el libro B tiene 30.

Sam sleeps more when he uses the phone more.
Sam uses the phone less when he sleeps less.

answer.text: far

feedback.es: By far + superlativo marca una gran distancia respecto a los demás equipos.

origin.text: Our team is by ___ the best in the school.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cuanto más lees, más palabras aprendes.»

answer.text: The more you read the more words you learn

feedback.es: Cada parte empieza con the + comparativo: the more …, the more ….

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase proporcional está bien formada?

choices.text: More you practise, more you improve.
The more you practise, the more you improve.
The more you practise, the more improve you.

feedback.es: Ambas partes necesitan the + comparativo y mantienen el orden sujeto + verbo.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuanto menos gastas, más ahorras.»

answer.text: less

feedback.es: Para cuanto menos se usa the less; la segunda parte sigue con the more.

origin.text: The ___ you spend, the more you save.

answer.text: School X has twice as many points as School Y.
accepted: School X has twice as many points as School Y.
School X scored twice as many points as School Y.

feedback.es: Treinta es el doble de quince: twice as many + sustantivo + as.

origin.text: Datos: la escuela X tiene 30 puntos y la escuela Y tiene 15.

choices.text: Drama has twice as many members as music.
Music has twice as many members as art.
Art has twice as many members as music.

title.en: What the survey can and can't say
title.es: Qué puede y qué no puede decir la encuesta

es: Distinguir lo que sugiere un estudio de lo que demuestra y detectar sus límites en un informe breve.

teaching.en: The study suggests that students who sleep more get better marks.
teaching.es: El estudio sugiere que los estudiantes que duermen más sacan mejores notas.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggests introduce una conclusión prudente: hay una relación posible, no una prueba.
segments: The study suggests that students who
teaching.audioText: The study suggests that students who sleep more get better marks.

teaching.en: This result does not prove that sleep is the only cause.
teaching.es: Este resultado no demuestra que el sueño sea la única causa.
teaching.explanationEs: Prove pide pruebas fuertes; con un solo estudio casi siempre se niega o se usa con cuidado.
segments: This result does not prove that
teaching.audioText: This result does not prove that sleep is the only cause.

teaching.en: The sample was small: only thirty participants answered.
teaching.es: La muestra era pequeña: solo respondieron treinta participantes.
teaching.explanationEs: La sample es el grupo que responde. Si es pequeña, el estudio tiene un límite.
teaching.audioText: The sample was small: only thirty participants answered.

teaching.en: There may be another factor, such as the time they go to bed.
teaching.es: Puede haber otro factor, como la hora a la que se acuestan.
teaching.explanationEs: May + be expresa posibilidad: no afirma el factor, solo lo admite.
segments: There may be another factor, such as
the time they go to bed.
teaching.audioText: There may be another factor, such as the time they go to bed.

teaching.en: The evidence supports a cautious conclusion, not a final answer.
teaching.es: La evidencia respalda una conclusión prudente, no una respuesta definitiva.
teaching.explanationEs: Cautious conclusion = conclusión con cuidado. Evidence no lleva plural.
teaching.audioText: The evidence supports a cautious conclusion, not a final answer.

teaching.en: The main limitation is that a link between two things is not always a cause.
teaching.es: La limitación principal es que una relación entre dos cosas no siempre es una causa.
teaching.explanationEs: Link es la relación entre dos datos; cause es lo que produce el otro.
segments: The main limitation is that a link between
two things is not always a cause.
teaching.audioText: The main limitation is that a link between two things is not always a cause.

The survey shows that every student sleeps well.

hint.es: Busca la conclusión más prudente: una relación, no una causa.

feedback.es: Does not prove that + causa niega que el estudio haya demostrado la causa.

hint.es: Usa does not prove y después that + sujeto + verbo.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la limitación principal de este estudio?

choices.text: The sample was small and all the participants were similar.
The questions were too easy for the participants.
The results were different from last year.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función: sugerir, negar una prueba, señalar un límite de tamaño o abrir otra explicación.

es: Escribir un informe breve con pregunta, muestra, resultados con proporción, una limitación y una conclusión prudente.

teaching.en: We asked one hundred students how many hours they sleep on school nights.
teaching.es: Preguntamos a cien estudiantes cuántas horas duermen las noches de colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta y muestra: asked + personas, sin to. Se cuenta en pasado lo que hicisteis.
segments: We asked one hundred students how many
hours they sleep on school nights.
teaching.audioText: We asked one hundred students how many hours they sleep on school nights.

teaching.en: Among the respondents, nearly half sleep less than seven hours.
teaching.es: Entre los encuestados, casi la mitad duerme menos de siete horas.
teaching.explanationEs: Nearly half da la proporción sin la cifra exacta. Los hallazgos van en presente.
teaching.audioText: Among the respondents, nearly half sleep less than seven hours.

teaching.en: Twice as many girls as boys said they feel tired in class.
teaching.es: El doble de chicas que de chicos dijo que se siente cansado en clase.
teaching.explanationEs: Un comparativo proporcional resume la diferencia entre dos grupos.
segments: Twice as many girls as boys
said they feel tired in class.
teaching.audioText: Twice as many girls as boys said they feel tired in class.

teaching.en: However, the main limitation is that all the respondents study at the same school.
teaching.es: Sin embargo, la limitación principal es que todos los encuestados estudian en el mismo colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: However + the main limitation is that … anuncia el punto débil del estudio.
segments: However, the main limitation is that all
the respondents study at the same school.
teaching.audioText: However, the main limitation is that all the respondents study at the same school.

teaching.en: The results suggest that late phone use may affect sleep, but more research is needed.
teaching.es: Los resultados sugieren que usar el móvil tarde puede afectar al sueño, pero hace falta más investigación.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest + may cierra con una conclusión prudente; more research is needed admite que aún no es definitiva.
segments: The results suggest that late phone use may
affect sleep, but more research is needed.

prompt.es: ¿Qué conclusión del informe es la más prudente?

The results prove that sleeping less lowers marks.

prompt.es: Escribe tu informe con los datos dados, de 70 a 170 palabras.

answer.text: We asked fifty students at our school how many hours they sleep on school nights. Nearly half of the respondents, twenty-two students, sleep less than seven hours. Twice as many girls as boys said they feel tired in class: sixteen girls and eight boys. However, the main limitation is that we asked students from only one school, so the results may be different in other schools. The sample is also small. In conclusion, the results suggest that sleeping less may make students feel tired, but more research is needed to be sure.
accepted: We asked fifty students at our school how many hours they sleep on school nights. Nearly half of the respondents, twenty-two students, sleep less than seven hours. Twice as many girls as boys said they feel tired in class: sixteen girls and eight boys. However, the main limitation is that we asked students from only one school, so the results may be different in other schools. The sample is also small. In conclusion, the results suggest that sleeping less may make students feel tired, but more research is needed to be sure.

We asked fifty students from our school about their sleep on school nights. Almost half of them, twenty-two students, sleep less than seven hours. Twice as many girls as boys feel tired in class: sixteen girls and eight boys. However, the main limitation is that we only asked one school, so the results may not be the same in other schools.
